Subject: Data residency questionnaire — region-level commitments

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement and security review we need a concise mapping showing which Redwood deployment modes and features allow us to keep data strictly within EU borders (including backups and logs), versus configurations that may require cross-border processing. Specifically:

- Can you confirm which hosted regions are physically located in the EU and whether we can restrict a tenant to EU-only storage and compute?
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, what contractual and technical controls prevent replication to non-EU regions?
- How are audit logs, metrics, and crash dumps handled — are they stored abroad by default?
- What is Redwood's subprocessors list and do you offer SCCs/UK Addendum?

We need a short, formal response we can include in our RFP packet. Can you also attach any standard clauses and the latest subprocessor list?

Thanks — Sylvie

HeliosBank

Sylvie — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a short region-capabilities matrix and our latest subprocessor inventory. High-level answers below; linking a follow-up with our security lead (Monica) and Jordan (SE) to confirm any contractual language you may need.

Executive summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): EU-hosted clusters are available in Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and Amsterdam (eu-west-1). Customers may restrict tenancy to those regions; we support EU-only configs for data at rest and compute.
- Dedicated: Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in customer-preferred EU regions; we enforce isolation and do not replicate tenant data to non-EU regions unless explicitly configured for DR.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): Full control; customer-managed network and storage. No Redwood-side replication by default.
- Logs & telemetry: By default, application logs and usage metrics associated with the tenant are stored in the same region as the tenant for Hosted EU tenants. Operational backups and long-term analytics may be routed to a central telemetry pipeline — see notes/assurances below.

Key attachments: Redwood_Data_Residency_Matrix_v3.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessor_List_2025.xlsx, SCCs-Redwood-2025.pdf (attached).

Next steps: Monica will confirm the exact contract language for the SCCs and data transfer commitments; Jordan will confirm how backups and metrics are scoped per tenant. If helpful we can produce a short one-page addendum for your RFP packet.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Redwood_Data_Residency_Matrix_v3.pdf; Redwood_Subprocessor_List_2025.xlsx)

Subject: RE: Data residency questionnaire — region-level commitments (internal)

Folks — here's suggested, slightly more formal language we can send back to Sylvie that maps to contractual commitments. Please review:

Proposed formal response (to include in RFP):
- Regional hosting: Redwood offers EU-hosted production regions in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) and eu-west-1 (Amsterdam). For Hosted customers we provide a tenant-scoped configuration that ensures all customer data at rest, compute, and model cache are provisioned within the selected EU region(s).
- Data transfers: Redwood will not transfer customer content or backups outside of the EU except when: (a) customer expressly requests cross-region replication for DR, (b) required by law, or (c) for security incident response where cross-border processing is necessary and documented. All other processing will be kept in-region.
- Backups, logs, and telemetry: For EU-hosted tenants, operational backups and primary audit logs are retained in EU storage services. Aggregated telemetry and anonymous metrics used for platform analytics may be processed outside the EU; customers can opt out of aggregated telemetry or request contractual restrictions.
- Subprocessors and SCCs: We maintain an up-to-date subprocessors list (attached). Redwood executes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with customers as part of our DPA and offers a UK Addendum on request.
- Private & Dedicated: Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments keep all data under customer control. Dedicated capacity deployed in EU regions will be contractually scoped to prevent replication to non-EU regions unless explicitly authorized by the customer.

Open items for legal review: exact wording for "will not transfer" -> we recommend "will not transfer except as permitted under section X of the DPA" to align with SCCs and lawful requests. Also recommend confirming retention windows for backups (default 90 days) and whether Helios needs shorter windows.

Comments? Monica
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SCCs-Redwood-2025.pdf)

Monica — looks good. A couple of technical clarifications to add into the one-pager:

- KV cache & model artifacts: For Hosted EU tenants we pin model artifacts and KV caches to EU-local storage; the inference runtime will not pull model weights from non-EU object stores.
- Cross-region failover: We support planned DR failover to a secondary EU region (e.g., eu-central-1 -> eu-west-1) under customer opt-in. Cross-continent failover (EU -> US/APAC) requires explicit contract amendment.
- Logs: Error-level crash dumps are redacted by default and only exported with customer authorization; operational traces are accessible to customers via the Console within the EU region.

I can draft the technical bullet points for the RFP addendum; happy to sync with legal for phrase-level edits.

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
